checked_ok.claim: Drizzle ORM 1.0 is still a release candidate on 2026-10-04: newest full RC is 1.0.0-rc.4 (2026-06-27), no stable 1.0 yet; exact pinning is the right way to use an RC.
0.45.3 is the current stable drizzle-orm (npm latest tag, published 2026-09-21); drizzle-kit latest is 0.31.11, rc tag 1.0.0-rc.4.
Applying migrations as a separate release step instead of at startup is right: Drizzle's migrator takes no lock against a second runner.
Squawk is current and actively released (v2.67.0 on 2026-10-04, v2.66.0 on 2026-09-23); its rules target statements that block reads or writes or break existing clients.
Running migrations with a lock timeout matches Squawk's safety requirements (short lock_timeout, retry when it hits).
'Önce genişlet, sonra daralt' is the established parallel change pattern (expand, migrate, contract).
PostgreSQL 18 is supported until 2030-11-14; current minor is 18.6.
PostgreSQL 19 is not released on 2026-10-04 (Beta 4 on 2026-09-24, RC planned early October, GA may follow in October), so '19 çıkınca hemen geçilmez' still applies.
uuidv7() is built into PostgreSQL 18 (optional shift interval argument); uuid_extract_version() and uuid_extract_timestamp() are also available.
Not using UUIDv7 as an external token fits RFC 9562: UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities and embedded timestamps are a small attack surface.
'Partition when the table outgrows server memory' is PostgreSQL's own rule of thumb.

Term id in the unique keys from day one is required for unique constraints on a partitioned table; an existing table can later be attached as a partition with a matching CHECK constraint to skip the validation scan.
Storing all times in UTC is what timestamptz does internally.

ICU tr-TR is available as an imported ICU collation (BCP 47 name with -x-icu, e.g. tr-TR-x-icu) or via CREATE COLLATION (provider = icu, locale = 'tr-TR'); a deterministic collation (the default) is right for sorting.
No PgBouncer for now and the job queue on a direct connection is right: pg-boss supports LISTEN/NOTIFY delivery, and LISTEN never works in PgBouncer transaction pooling.
Adding PgBouncer later will not break prepared statements: protocol-level named prepared statements since 1.21, on by default (max_prepared_statements 200) since 1.24; latest is 1.26.0 (2026-09-23).
Nightly pg_dump next to physical backups is right-sized: pg_dump is logical and cannot be part of point-in-time recovery, so the two cover different failures.
pgBackRest is maintained and current: 2.59.3 released 2026-10-04; PostgreSQL 19 support since 2.59.0 (2026-07-20).
50,000 x 6 x 1 x 28 = 8,400,000 records per year (arithmetic checked).
20,000 requests over 300 s is about 67/s and over 60 s about 333/s, so '70 to 330 per second' is right (arithmetic checked).
Valkey is current and maintained (9.1.2 on 2026-08-31, 9.0.6 on 2026-09-01, 9.2.0-rc1 on 2026-09-16); deferring it until there is more than one API copy is correct.
@fastify/rate-limit uses an in-memory store by default and needs an external store only when the app runs on multiple servers, which is exactly when the plan adds Valkey.

findings.plan_quote: sorun çıkarsa 0.45.3'e dönülür
findings.finding: Drizzle 1.0 is still RC on 2026-10-04 (newest full RC 1.0.0-rc.4 of 2026-06-27; npm latest 0.45.3 of 2026-09-21; drizzle-kit latest 0.31.11, rc 1.0.0-rc.4). Staying on the RC is defensible (the Drizzle docs now install drizzle-orm@rc). The stated fallback is the weak part: once code and migrations exist, going back to 0.45.3 is not cheap. rc.1 removed relational queries v1 (db._query) for postgres, so 1.0 code uses defineRelations, which 0.45 lacks; the casing API moved from the db instance to tables; and v1 changed the migrations folder format (no journal.json, one folder per migration, new name and applied_at columns in __drizzle_migrations), built for drizzle-kit v1. A rollback means rewriting relation definitions and relational queries and rebuilding the migration baseline.

evidence.quote: Removed RQBv1 (`db._query`) from `postgres`
No more `journal.json` ... SQL files and snapshots grouped into separate migration folders.

findings.recommendation_tr: Drizzle 1.0 RC'de kalırım ve sürümü tam sabitlerim (şu an 1.0.0-rc.4). '0.45.3'e dönülür' cümlesini düzeltirim: bu dönüş yalnız ilk göçler ve sorgular yazılmadan önce ucuzdur; sonrasında ilişki tanımları ve göç klasörü biçimi farklı olduğu için yeniden yazım ister. Sorun çıkarsa önce bir önceki RC'ye ya da düzeltme sürümüne geçerim. Sorgularda olabildiğince temel sorgu kurucuyu (select, insert, update) kullanırım ki sürüm farkı az iz bıraksın. 1.0 kararlı çıkınca ona geçerim.

findings.plan_quote: Squawk ile denetle, drizzle-kit check, sonra açılışta değil ayrı bir yayın adımı olarak uygula
findings.finding: Drizzle's migrator runs all pending migrations inside one transaction, with no opt-out and no lock against a second runner; this is in the 1.0 beta branch source as well as in 0.45, and issues #860 (CONCURRENTLY, opened 2023-07-04) and #3249 (several files in one transaction, opened 2024-10-29) are still open. Effects on the plan's flow: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot go through the migrator, so for every index on an existing table Squawk will fire either require-concurrent-index-creation or ban-concurrent-index-creation-in-transaction; a value added with ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE cannot be used in the same run, and enum values cannot be removed without re-creating the type. Squawk needs --assume-in-transaction to model the wrapper. Squawk's safety rules also ask for lock_timeout plus statement_timeout and a retry when the lock timeout hits; the plan names only the lock timeout.

evidence.quote: await db.transaction(async (tx) => { for (const migration of migrationsToRun) {
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block
Another difference is that a regular CREATE INDEX command can be performed within a transaction block, but CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot.
If ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (the form that adds a new value to an enum type) is executed inside a transaction block, the new value cannot be used until after the transaction has been committed.
Existing values cannot be removed from an enum type, nor can the sort ordering of such values be changed, short of dropping and re-creating the enum type.
If your migration hits the lock timeout, it will be cancelled and error, allowing the waiting queries to proceed. You should retry a migration that hits the lock timeout until it succeeds.
Assume that a transaction will wrap each SQL file when run by a migration tool.

findings.recommendation_tr: Drizzle bekleyen bütün göçleri tek işlemde çalıştırdığı için göç kurallarımı buna göre yazarım. Squawk 'işlem içinde çalışır' ayarıyla (--assume-in-transaction) çalışır. Her göç dosyası kilit ve komut zaman aşımıyla başlar (SET LOCAL lock_timeout ve statement_timeout); zaman aşımında göç yeniden denenir. Dolu bir tabloya dizin gerekirse o komutu göç aracının dışında CONCURRENTLY ile ayrı çalıştırırım; küçük tablolarda dizini ders saatleri dışında normal eklerim ve Squawk'ın dizin kuralını buna göre ayarlarım. Durum ve etiket gibi değer listeleri PostgreSQL enum değil, metin ve CHECK kısıtıdır; enum'a eklenen değer aynı işlemde kullanılamıyor ve değer silinemiyor.

findings.plan_quote: drizzle-kit check
findings.finding: In Drizzle v1, drizzle-kit check only checks the consistency of the generated migration history: it builds a DAG from snapshot prevIds and reports non-commutative migrations across branches. It does not compare the TypeScript schema with the last snapshot, so a schema edit committed without running generate passes this gate. v1 generate already runs the same commutativity check by default (--ignore-conflicts skips it). A regenerate-and-diff step, which the plan already uses for OpenAPI, catches the forgotten migration with no new tool.

evidence.quote: check consistency of your generated SQL migrations history
builds a DAG from snapshot `prevIds` ... non-commutative migrations across branches
skip commutativity conflict checks, default is `false`

findings.recommendation_tr: drizzle-kit check yalnız dallar arasındaki göç çakışmasını yakalar; şemayı değiştirip göç üretmeyi unutmayı yakalamaz. CI'da göçleri yeniden üretirim (drizzle-kit generate); yeni göç dosyası çıkarsa CI durur. OpenAPI için yaptığımın aynısı, yeni araç gerekmez.

findings.plan_quote: Yoklama kaydının kimliğini telefon üretir ve bu aynı zamanda tekrar gönderme anahtarıdır
findings.finding: A client-chosen UUID used as the idempotency key needs guards the plan does not state. (1) Fingerprint: if the same id arrives with different signed bytes or from another device, answering 'zaten var' silently drops a real record; the IETF Idempotency-Key draft says to reject a reused key with a different payload and to look up on a composite of the key and client attributes. (2) Validate the key format: CHECK (uuid_extract_version(id) = 7) is cheap. (3) Never use the timestamp inside the id: it comes from the phone clock, which the plan distrusts, and PostgreSQL notes the extracted timestamp is not necessarily the generation time. (4) With three unique rules on one table (id, device+seq, session+student), a 200-record batch using ON CONFLICT on one target still raises on the other indexes and aborts the whole transaction; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING without a target handles all unique indexes, after which each record is classified. Minor wording: UUIDv7 is 16 bytes like v4; its gain is index locality, not small indexes, and ids arriving up to 7 days late keep that gain only in part.

evidence.quote: If there is an attempt to reuse an idempotency key with a different request payload, the resource SHOULD reply with a HTTP 422 status code with body containing a link pointing to relevant documentation.

On the resource, implement a unique composite key as the idempotent cache lookup key. For example, a composite key MAY be implemented by combining the idempotency key sent by the client with other client specific attributes known only to the resource.
Note that the extracted timestamp is not necessarily exactly equal to the time the UUID was generated; this depends on the implementation that generated the UUID.
For ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, it is optional to specify a conflict_target; when omitted, conflicts with all usable constraints (and unique indexes) are handled.
UUID versions that are not time ordered, such as UUIDv4 ... have poor database-index locality.

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefonun ürettiği kimlik tekrar gönderme anahtarı olarak kalır, şu kurallarla: Aynı kimlik farklı imzalı baytla ya da başka cihazdan gelirse 'zaten var' değil 'ret' döner ve kayıt işaretlenir. Kimliğin UUIDv7 olduğu veritabanında denetlenir (uuid_extract_version(id) = 7). Kimliğin içindeki zaman hiçbir hesapta kullanılmaz; kayıt zamanı saat belgesinden gelir. Paket eklerken çakışma hedefi vermeden 'çakışırsa ekleme' (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) kullanırım ki tekil kurallardan biri bütün paketi düşürmesin; sonra her kayda ayrı sonuç dönerim. Plandaki 'dizinleri küçük' yerine 'dizine sırayla eklenir' yazarım.

findings.plan_quote: bir oturumda bir öğrenciye tek kayıt
findings.finding: A hard UNIQUE (session, student) on the raw attendance records conflicts with flows the plan describes: pending records from the old phone are decided together with the new phone's records after a device change (line 233), and in Aşama 2 two started sessions merge into one (line 255), which produces duplicate (session, student) pairs. The second validly signed record would be rejected and its evidence lost. PostgreSQL's documented pattern for this is a partial unique index: one 'successful' row per key, any number of others. The same tool enforces 'one active device per student' (line 84), which the constraint list omits.

evidence.quote: We wish to ensure that there is only one “successful” entry for a given subject and target combination, but there might be any number of “unsuccessful” entries.

findings.recommendation_tr: Ham yoklama kayıtları kanıttır; aynı oturum ve öğrenci için birden çok olabilir (cihaz değişimi, birleşen oturum). 'Bir oturumda bir öğrenciye tek kayıt' kuralını yalnız sayılan kayıtta kısmi tekil dizinle korurum (WHERE sayıldı); diğerleri saklanır ve hocaya gösterilir. Aynı yolla 'bir öğrencide tek etkin cihaz' kuralı da veritabanında korunur.

findings.plan_quote: Tablo sunucunun belleğinden büyüyünce döneme göre bölünür; tahmin yılda
findings.finding: The row count is right (50,000 x 6 x 28 = 8,400,000 a year), but '1 to 3 GB a year' fits only the heap of a lean row. Using PostgreSQL's documented layout (23-byte tuple header, 4-byte line pointer, 8 kB pages): a lean row (UUID ids, term, seq, three timestamps, label flags, a 64-byte ES256 signature) is about 210 bytes, about 38 rows per page, about 1.8 GB of heap a year; the four B-tree indexes the plan implies (id, device+seq, session+student, student) add about 1.5 GB, so about 3.5 GB a year in total. If each row also keeps the exact signed bytes (a compact JWS of roughly 0.8 to 1 KB that also carries the time certificate), rows stay under the 2 kB TOAST threshold and are stored uncompressed: about 7 to 8 rows per page, about 9 GB of heap, about 10 to 11 GB a year with indexes. One PostgreSQL still holds this, but the 'outgrows memory' point for partitioning and the backup size arrive up to about 3 times sooner. Hand estimate from documented sizes, to be confirmed by measurement.

evidence.quote: All table rows are structured in the same way. There is a fixed-size header (occupying 23 bytes on most machines), followed by an optional null bitmap, an optional object ID field, and the user data.
The TOAST management code is triggered only when a row value to be stored in a table is wider than TOAST_TUPLE_THRESHOLD bytes (normally 2 kB).
The resulting 64-octet sequence is the JWS Signature value.

findings.recommendation_tr: Boyut tahminini satır boyutuna göre düzeltirim: yalın satırla dizinler dahil yılda yaklaşık 3,5 GB; imzalı ham baytlar da saklanırsa yaklaşık 10 GB. Yük testinden sonra tablonun gerçek boyutunu ölçer (pg_total_relation_size) ve plana yazarım. Bölme kararı yine 'tablo belleği aşınca' kuralıyla verilir.

findings.plan_quote: saat belgesi, imza
findings.finding: The plan signs the exact bytes (JWS ES256) to avoid re-serialization errors (line 589). A JWS signature can only be re-verified against the exact signing input (base64url header, '.', base64url payload). Storing the signature and the time certificate as separate columns next to parsed fields does not allow later re-verification (a dispute, or a key later found weak) unless the exact bytes are kept. If the exact signed bytes are stored once, the separate signature and certificate columns are redundant because both are inside those bytes.

evidence.quote: JWS Signing Input: The input to the digital signature or MAC computation. Its value is ASCII(BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)) || '.' || BASE64URL(JWS Payload)).

findings.recommendation_tr: Yoklama kaydında telefonun imzaladığı ham baytları bir kez, olduğu gibi saklarım. Saat belgesi ve imza bu baytların içinde olduğu için ayrı sütun olmaz; sorgulanan alanlar (kimlik, oturum, hesaplanan saat, etiketler) ayrıca sütundur. Böylece imza yıllar sonra da yeniden doğrulanabilir.

findings.plan_quote: raporlar için kayıt zamanında hafif bir aralık dizini (BRIN)
findings.finding: BRIN only helps when the column correlates with physical row order. Rows are written in arrival order, but the record time can be up to 7 days earlier (offline sending, line 136; target is only 95% within 24 h, line 830), so most block ranges will hold some late rows and each range's min/max summary widens to days, and the index skips little. New ranges are also left unsummarized until a summarization run unless autosummarize is on, which it is not by default. Reports by course, student and date range can go through sessions (the date lives on the session) and the (session, student) and student indexes the table needs anyway; the plan's own rule is indexes from real queries.

evidence.quote: BRIN is designed for handling very large tables in which certain columns have some natural correlation with their physical location within the table.

Also, if the index's autosummarize parameter is enabled, which it isn't by default, whenever autovacuum runs in that database, summarization will occur for all unsummarized page ranges that have been filled

findings.recommendation_tr: BRIN'i baştan koymam. Raporlar oturum üzerinden çalışır (tarih oturumda) ve zaten gereken (oturum, öğrenci) ve öğrenci dizinlerini kullanır. Gerçek bir tarih aralığı sorgusu yavaşlarsa sunucuya ulaşma zamanına BRIN eklerim; o sütun ekleme sırasıyla gider.

findings.plan_quote: İsim sıralaması Türkçe kurallarla (ICU tr-TR) yapılır.
findings.finding: Syntax is fine (ORDER BY ad COLLATE "tr-TR-x-icu", or CREATE COLLATION with provider = icu, locale = 'tr-TR'; deterministic is right for sorting, nondeterministic costs speed and B-tree deduplication). Caveats the plan omits: (1) when the ICU library changes (new OS or image), every index using that collation must be rebuilt and the collation version refreshed; (2) the official Debian image runs with en_US.utf8, so by default the cluster uses libc collation and every text index depends on glibc locale data, while the builtin C.UTF-8 locale is stable within a major version; the database default can only be chosen at creation; (3) builtin collations sort by code point, so they cannot replace tr-TR for names; (4) lower() and upper() follow the database locale, so tr-TR as the database default would apply Turkish I/ı casing to fields like e-mail. Also 'UTC' needs timestamptz columns: Drizzle's timestamp() defaults to without time zone (withTimezone: true is needed), and Squawk's prefer-timestamptz rule catches it.

evidence.quote: When this happens, all objects depending on the collation should be rebuilt, for example, using REINDEX. When that is done, the collation version can be refreshed using the command ALTER COLLATION ... REFRESH VERSION.
This collation sorts by Unicode code point values rather than natural language order. ... Behavior is efficient and stable within a PostgreSQL major version.
These initialization files will be executed in sorted name order as defined by the current locale, which defaults to `en_US.utf8`.
Databases or table columns using the 'C' or 'POSIX' locales are not affected. All other locales are potentially affected.
Converts the string to all lower case, according to the rules of the database's locale.
When Postgres stores a datetime in a timestamp field, Postgres drops the UTC offset.

findings.recommendation_tr: Zaman sütunları timestamptz olur (Drizzle'da withTimezone: true); Squawk'ın prefer-timestamptz kuralı bunu denetler. Veritabanını ilk kurulumda builtin C.UTF-8 yereliyle açarım (POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS); bu karar sonradan değişmez ve bu sıralama bir PostgreSQL ana sürümü içinde sabittir. Türkçe kuralı yalnız isim sıralamasında kullanırım: ORDER BY ad COLLATE "tr-TR-x-icu". İsim sütununa bu kuralla dizin koymam; böylece işletim sistemi ya da ICU güncellemesinde yeniden dizinleme gerekmez. tr-TR'yi veritabanının varsayılanı yapmam, çünkü büyük küçük harf dönüşümü de varsayılan yerele göre yapılır.

findings.plan_quote: Düzeltmeler ve onaylar ayrı tabloya yazılır, silinmez.
findings.finding: 'Silinmez' is only a code promise unless the database enforces it, which falls short of line 615 ('Kodda hata olsa bile bozuk veri yazılamaz'). In PostgreSQL the right to modify or drop an object belongs to its owner and cannot be revoked; if the API connects as the role that ran the migrations, it can always UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE the audit table. Two roles (migration owner; application role with only the grants it needs, on the audit table only INSERT and SELECT) make the table append-only with no extra tool. The test reset that empties tables (line 644) then runs as the owner role.

evidence.quote: The right to modify or destroy an object is inherent in being the object's owner, and cannot be granted or revoked in itself.
For most kinds of objects, the initial state is that only the owner (or a superuser) can do anything with the object.

findings.recommendation_tr: Veritabanında iki rol olur: göçleri çalıştıran sahip rol ve uygulamanın bağlandığı rol. Uygulama rolü denetim tablosunda yalnız ekleme ve okuma yapabilir (INSERT, SELECT); güncelleme, silme ve boşaltma izni yoktur. Böylece 'silinmez' kuralı kod hatasında da korunur. Testlerde tabloları boşaltma işini sahip rol yapar.

findings.plan_quote: pgBackRest ile istenen ana geri dönülebilen yedek
findings.finding: pgBackRest is maintained today but nearly stopped in 2026: on 2026-04-27 its maintainer announced it was no longer maintained; on 2026-05-18 development resumed with backing from several companies, and a second maintainer is only planned. On 2026-10-04 version 2.59.3 fixed weak encryption subkeys and salts in encrypted repositories made by earlier versions. By the plan's own rule (line 741: packages with a single maintainer get a named fallback) it belongs on that list. A fallback with no new dependency exists: PostgreSQL's own pg_basebackup (incremental since 17) plus WAL archiving; nightly pg_dump stays as the independent logical copy. Operational note: archive_command runs pgBackRest on the database host, so the PostgreSQL container needs pgBackRest installed.

evidence.quote: After a lot of thought, I have decided to stop working on pgBackRest. I did not come to this decision lightly.
I am pleased to announce that pgBackRest will continue!
Versions of pgBackRest prior to 2.59.3 did not check for an error when generating random data for encryption.
You can use pg_basebackup to take an incremental backup by specifying the --incremental option.
archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=demo archive-push %p'

findings.recommendation_tr: pgBackRest kalır, sürümü 2.59.3 ve üstü olur. Proje Nisan 2026'da bırakılıp Mayıs 2026'da şirket desteğiyle yeniden başladığı için 'tek kişinin bakımındaki araçlar' listesine eklerim; yedeği PostgreSQL'in kendi araçlarıdır (pg_basebackup ve WAL arşivi), ek paket gerekmez. Gecelik pg_dump bağımsız ikinci kopya olarak kalır. pgBackRest, arşiv komutunu çalıştırabilsin diye PostgreSQL kabına kurulur.

findings.plan_quote: ayrıca gecelik pg_dump ve düzenli geri yükleme denemesi
findings.finding: The plan does not say where backups live or how fresh the WAL archive is. With one Docker Compose host, a repository on the same disk is lost together with the database. pgBackRest supports s3, sftp, gcs and azure repositories and AES-256 repository encryption. WAL is archived only per completed segment (16 MB by default); at this write volume a segment can stay open for a long time, so 'istenen an' is only as fresh as the last archived segment unless archive_timeout is set; PostgreSQL says about a minute is usually reasonable.

evidence.quote: Hence, if your server generates little WAL traffic (or has slack periods where it does so), there could be a long delay between the completion of a transaction and its safe recording in archive storage.
archive_timeout settings of a minute or so are usually reasonable.
s3 - AWS Simple Storage Service ... sftp - Secure File Transfer Protocol ... aes-256-cbc - Advanced Encryption Standard with 256 bit key length

findings.recommendation_tr: Yedek deposu sunucunun dışında olur (S3 uyumlu bir depo ya da SFTP ile başka bir makine) ve şifrelenir; gecelik pg_dump da oraya gider. WAL arşivi en geç dakikada bir kapanır (archive_timeout = 60 s); böylece istenen ana dönüşte en çok yaklaşık bir dakikalık veri risktedir.

findings.plan_quote: istenen ana geri dönülebilen yedek
findings.finding: Even with archiving, a restore loses what was committed after the last archived WAL. Records acknowledged in that window (student already saw 'Sunucuya ulaştı') vanish from the server, which breaks the plan's own target 'Kayıt kaybı 0: Makbuzu olup sunucuda bulunmayan kayıt çıkmamalı' (lines 841-842). The plan already has what closes this without a new component: the unique (device, sequence number). If phones keep acknowledged records until the term is locked and the server reports, on each sync, the last sequence number it holds for that device, a phone resends everything above it after a restore. Phones send in order (line 127), so a restore cuts a tail per device, which this rule covers.

evidence.quote: The archive_command or archive_library is only invoked for completed WAL segments.

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefon, sunucuya ulaşan kayıtlarını da dönem kilitlenene kadar saklar. Sunucu her eşitlemede o cihazdan aldığı son sıra numarasını bildirir; telefonda daha büyük numaralı onaylı kayıt varsa yeniden gönderir. Böylece yedekten dönüşte bile makbuzu olan kayıt kaybolmaz; yeni parça gerekmez, (cihaz, sıra numarası) zaten var.

findings.plan_quote: hesaplanan saat, telefon saati, etiket
findings.finding: The record row lacks the server arrival time, which the plan relies on: arrival sets the latest possible time of a record (line 186), the 7-day limit and the 'sonradan değişenler' list depend on it (line 136), and the 95%-within-24-hours target is measured with it (line 830). It also lacks the server decision and its reason code (var, incelemede, ret). One 'etiket' field cannot hold the combinations the plan uses at once (QR'sız plus Cihaz doğrulanmadı plus Beklemede, lines 196-217); separate yes/no columns with CHECK constraints are simpler to query and enforce than one value.

evidence.quote: A check constraint is the most generic constraint type. It allows you to specify that the value in a certain column must satisfy a Boolean (truth-value) expression.
In either case, the value is stored internally as UTC, and the originally stated or assumed time zone is not retained.

findings.recommendation_tr: Yoklama kaydına sunucuya ulaşma zamanı, sunucunun kararı ve gerekçe kodu eklenir; 7 gün kuralı, 'en geç zaman' kanıtı ve 24 saat hedefi bu alanla ölçülür. Etiketler aynı anda birden çok olabildiği için tek alan değil ayrı evet/hayır alanlarıdır (QR'sız, kendi beyanı, beklemede, saat doğrulanamadı, cihaz doğrulanmadı).

findings.plan_quote: hangi öğrenci hangi derste; aktif ya da pasif, muaf mı
findings.finding: The add-drop rule (line 385: weeks before a student was added are not counted, the instructor can change this) cannot be computed from an active/passive flag; the list row needs the date added, the date made passive and who changed it. The person model also needs the first-registration confirmation state (who confirmed, when; lines 74-75), since records stay 'beklemede' until then. Better Auth, used for instructor e-mail codes, brings its own user, session, account and verification tables; the instructor row links to the Better Auth user.

evidence.quote: Better Auth requires the following tables to be present in the database.

findings.recommendation_tr: Ders listesi satırına listeye eklenme tarihi, pasif olma tarihi ve değiştiren kişi eklenir; ekle-bırak kuralı bu tarihlerle hesaplanır. Öğrenci kaydında ilk kayıt teyidi tutulur (teyit eden hoca, tarih). Better Auth'un kendi dört tablosu (kullanıcı, oturum, hesap, doğrulama) da şemadadır; hoca kaydı Better Auth kullanıcısına bağlanır.

findings.plan_quote: açık anahtarları, anahtar türü (donanım ya da yazılım) ve doğrulama sonucu
findings.finding: App Attest assertion checks require the server to store the last counter per key and verify each new assertion's counter is greater (the plan relies on this: line 683, 'her kayıt için artan sayaçlı onay'); the device row has no such column. The device row should also hold the last sequence number received from that device, which turns the unique (device, seq) into replay and gap detection and supports the restore resend in S03-F13.

evidence.quote: Verify that the authenticator data's counter value is greater than the value from the previous assertion, or greater than 0 on the first assertion.
Store counter to use in step 5 when verifying the next assertion.

findings.recommendation_tr: Cihaz kaydına iki alan eklenir: App Attest'in son sayaç değeri (her yeni onayda sayaç büyümeli, Apple bunu şart koşuyor) ve o cihazdan alınan son sıra numarası. Böylece tekrar oynatılan ya da arada kaybolan kayıt fark edilir.

findings.plan_quote: Veri modeli (ilk taslak)
findings.finding: Line 133 says schedules and lists are downloaded as 'changes since version N' and deleted rows arrive with a deleted flag, but the data model has neither a change-version column nor tombstones on the synced tables (courses, schedule hours, sessions, lists, holidays). The version must also be assigned so that a transaction committing late cannot land below a version a phone already passed; a sequence value or timestamp taken inside the transaction does not guarantee that. PostgreSQL gives a safe rule: store the writing transaction id (pg_current_xact_id) and hand phones the current snapshot's xmin as the next watermark, since every transaction below xmin is finished. For rare writes, serializing them through one counter row is the simpler alternative.

evidence.quote: Lowest transaction ID that was still active. All transaction IDs less than xmin are either committed and visible, or rolled back and dead.
Returns the current transaction's ID. It will assign a new one if the current transaction does not have one already (because it has not performed any database updates)

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefona inen tablolarda (dersler, ders saatleri, oturumlar, listeler, tatiller) her satırda bir değişiklik sürümü ve 'silindi' işareti olur; satır silinmez, işaretlenir. Sürüm, aynı anda yapılan iki değişiklikte biri atlanmayacak biçimde verilir: işlem kimliği ve 'bitmemiş en eski işlem' sınırıyla (pg_current_xact_id, pg_snapshot_xmin) ya da bu tablolara yazmayı tek bir sayaç satırıyla sıraya sokarak.

findings.plan_quote: Olay kaydı: gönderme ve hata ölçümleri.
findings.finding: The metrics named in line 151 (send rate, share with unverified time, share flagged) and the 24-hour target can be computed from the attendance table once it stores arrival time, computed time and label flags; one aggregate query with FILTER gives the rates. A separate raw event table on the server would duplicate that data and grow with every send attempt. Only what the server cannot see (records still unsent on phones, failed attempts) has to come from phones, as small daily counters.

evidence.quote: If FILTER is specified, then only the input rows for which the filter_clause evaluates to true are fed to the aggregate function; other rows are discarded.

findings.recommendation_tr: Ayrı bir ham olay tablosu tutmam. Gönderme süresi, saati doğrulanamayan ve işaretli oranlar yoklama kayıtlarından tek sorguyla hesaplanır. Telefondan yalnız sunucunun göremediği sayılar gelir (gönderilmeyi bekleyen kayıt, başarısız deneme), günlük toplam olarak.

findings.plan_quote: PostgreSQL 18. 19 çıkınca hemen geçilmez.
findings.finding: Two PostgreSQL 18 details are missing. (1) In the official Docker image, PGDATA for 18 is /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and the VOLUME moved to /var/lib/postgresql; a Compose file that mounts its volume at the old /var/lib/postgresql/data does not hold the data (it lands in an anonymous volume), and pgBackRest settings must use the new path. (2) PostgreSQL recommends always running the current minor release (18.6 now); the plan only names the major. The '19 not immediately' rule itself is right (see checked items).

evidence.quote: the `PGDATA` environment variable of the image was changed to be version specific in PostgreSQL 18 and above. For 18 it is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`.
The defined `VOLUME` was changed in 18 and above to `/var/lib/postgresql`.
We recommend that users always run the current minor release associated with their major version.

findings.recommendation_tr: Compose'da PostgreSQL verisini /var/lib/postgresql yoluna bağlarım (18 ile veri yolu /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker oldu); pgBackRest ayarı da bu yolu kullanır. İmajı tam ara sürümle sabitlerim (şu an 18.6) ve yeni ara sürümleri çıktıkça uygularım; 19'a geçiş yine bekler.

findings.plan_quote: Yoklama tablosunun tekil anahtarlarında dönem kimliği baştan yer alır.
findings.finding: Keeping the term id in every unique key is the right preparation. The consequence the plan does not state: a foreign key must reference a primary key, unique constraint or non-partial unique index, so tables pointing at an attendance record (corrections, issue reports, audit) must reference (term id, record id). If someone adds a unique constraint on the record id alone to make a simple foreign key, the table can no longer be partitioned by term without rework.

evidence.quote: If the refcolumn list is omitted, the primary key of the reftable is used. Otherwise, the refcolumn list must refer to the columns of a non-deferrable unique or primary key constraint or be the columns of a non-partial unique index.

To create a unique or primary key constraint on a partitioned table, the partition keys must not include any expressions or function calls and the constraint's columns must include all of the partition key columns.

findings.recommendation_tr: Yoklama kaydına başvuran tablolar (düzeltme, sorun bildirimi, denetim) kayda (dönem, kimlik) çiftiyle başvurur; yalnız kimlik üzerinde tekil kısıt açmam. Böylece tablo ileride döneme bölünürken yeniden yazım gerekmez.

compactness_notes: No new tool is recommended anywhere in this slice. Removals and merges: drop the BRIN pre-commitment (minus 1 index); merge 'saat belgesi' and 'imza' into one stored signed-bytes column (minus 1 to 2 columns); replace a raw server event table with rates computed from attendance rows plus small daily counters from phones (minus 1 growing table); keep PgBouncer, Valkey and the read replica deferred as the plan already does. Additions only use what the plan already has: columns and constraints (arrival time, decision, label flags, list dates, confirmation state, App Attest counter and last sequence per device, sync version and deleted flag), two database roles, one CI regenerate step with drizzle-kit, Squawk settings (--assume-in-transaction, timeouts), archive_timeout and an off-machine pgBackRest repository. pgBackRest stays; its named fallback is PostgreSQL's own pg_basebackup and WAL archiving, so no new dependency. Net moving parts: 0 tools added; 1 index, 1 to 2 columns and possibly 1 table removed. Capacity figures in S03-F06 are hand estimates from documented PostgreSQL sizes (the owner barred scripts), so they are marked medium confidence and should be confirmed by measuring after the load test.
